message.content:
I don’t have a way to probe your connection from here, so I can’t tell you the exact numbers.  
But you can get a quick read‑out yourself with a few simple steps:

---

## 1. Use an online speed‑test website  
The easiest way is to visit one of the popular sites:

| Site | How to use |
|------|------------|
| **Speedtest by Ookla** | <https://www.speedtest.net> – click “Go” and wait for the test to finish. |
| **Fast.com** | <https://fast.com> – it starts automatically and shows download speed; click “Show more info” for upload and latency. |
| **Google Speed Test** | Search “speed test” on Google and click the “Run Speed Test” button that appears in the search results. |

These sites give you download speed, upload speed, and ping (latency).

---

## 2. Run a command‑line test (Windows)

If you prefer a terminal/PowerShell approach, you can use the free **speedtest‑cli** tool.  
Below are two ways to get it running:

### a) Quick one‑liner (no installation needed)

```powershell
powershell -Command "(New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/speedtest-cli/speedtest-cli/master/speedtest.py') | python -"
```

*What it does:*  
- Downloads the `speedtest.py` script from GitHub.  
- Pipes it straight into Python, which runs the test and prints the results.

> **Prerequisite:** Python must be installed and in your PATH.  
> If you don’t have Python, you can install it from <https://www.python.org/downloads/> (make sure to tick “Add Python to PATH”).

### b) Install the package (recommended for repeated use)

```powershell
# 1. Install the package (requires pip)
pip install speedtest-cli

# 2. Run a simple test
speedtest-cli --simple
```

*Output will look like:*

```
Ping: 12.34 ms
Download: 123.45 Mbit/s
Upload: 67.89 Mbit/s
```

---

## 3. Check your router or ISP dashboard

Many modern routers expose a “Status” or “Internet” page that shows current throughput.  
If you’re on a cable or fiber plan, the ISP’s portal (e.g., Comcast Xfinity, Verizon FiOS, AT&T Fiber) often has a built‑in speed test as well.

---

### Quick recap

| Method | When to use | What you’ll see |
|--------|-------------|-----------------|
| Web site (speedtest.net, fast.com) | One‑off, quick check | Download, upload, ping |
| PowerShell one‑liner | No Python install, single run | Same metrics |
| `speedtest-cli` CLI | Repeated tests, scripting | Same metrics, plus optional JSON output |

Pick whichever feels most convenient for you. If you run into any hiccups (e.g., “Python not found” or “pip not recognized”), let me know and I can walk you through the fix!
